Messages.Author: Eric Freeman
Messages.Body:
After following the threads on how to mutualy withdraw. I have a question.
Can someone please give me one solid reason why this rule needs to exist in
the first place? I have been playing Jyhad since 1994 and I have never seen
a sucessful withdraw in casual play. To be honest I can't recall it ever
being attempted. The only time I've even heard of it done is the whole lets
all withdraw so I can advance crap that seems to be in vouge this year. The
rule serves no purpose whatsoever. Except as a loophole for whiney players
who misjudged the tounament metagame. If you deserve to be in the finals
then you should be able to OUST YOUR PREY! If you can't do that then you
don't deserve to advance. We don't need several pages of new tounament rules
so an entire table can quit with no repercussions. The withdraw rule should
be eliminated entirely.

Eric Freeman

Would you like some cheese to go with your whine?

> I never said it couldn't be done. I do see some strategic implications of a

You suggest that the rule be done away with because you have never seen its

by the inevitable posts that will be made to point out such errors.

> and how to cope with it conversation still bugs me. seems to me that it

Successfully withdrawing is a rare case, yes. The effect of being able to
attempt to withdraw is more pervasive, however. It, like gaining pool for
having the edge at the beginning of your turn, is part of the game to help
prevent the game from stalling out as player entrench and wait for other
players to stick their necks out. The rule exists to encourage proactive
play.

> added complication required to keep it from being abused? When entire tables
> are agreeing to not play the game that to me is a big problem. that far

Entire tables agreeing to withdraw is not an example of entire tables
agreeing not to play the game. Withdrawing is part of the game, and the
agreement to withdraw can only come (under the play to win rule) after
the vast majority of the game has been played.

> outweighs the minor benefit a single player can gain from using the rule in
> a contentious manner.

I wouldn't call improving one's final standing in the finals of a tournament
a minor benefit.

Your use of "contentious" is puzzling. Please enlighten me as to the
"contentiousness" of the play.

Messages.Author: David Cherryholmes
Messages.Body:
There was another instance of the withdrawal rule coming into play at
DragonCon. We were playing a four way, I had the table under an iron fist
with a multi-rush deck, when my prey squeeked through an oust, leaving us
at a three-way that I was going to obviously win. My predator tells me
that if I agree to let him withdraw he won't influence himself out,
otherwise he would. He had no minions, he was meat. If he withdrew then
my prey would've had two VP's and the best I could get was a tie. With
his deal I got the tablewin, and he got one more VP than he would've.

Messages.Author: Wouter Kuyper
Messages.Body:
Ok, i thought i would post it in this thread.

I think the withdrawal rule is good and it adds strategic options to
the game.

that's one.

BUT,

It happens very often (i use it as well) that just before timelimit, a
whole table decides to withdraw increasing each persons VP from 0,5 to
1.

I don't think the withdrawal rule was meant to be used like that
(speculation) and it also gives me a feeling of abusing the rules.

I think that if a table goes towards timelimit the players deserve to
get only the 0.5 VP they would get for surviving until then.

As LSJ pointed out to me in a private mail the problem lies maybe not
within the withdrawal rule, but in the Time Limit. He is right
(ofcourse), but i think time limit is a given in tournament play.

This means that i think the withdrawal rule should be changed in such
a way that it leaves all the strategic options open, but that it
leaves out the option of an escape route for everyone just before the
timelimit passes.

I haven't given it much thought yet, but would it be reasonable to
assume that it happens VERY little that 2 or more players attempt to
withdraw in a single game, where it s not used as an escape route for
the timelimit?

So my idea would be the following:
Only one player per game can succesfully withdraw.

It might have repercussions on Brinksmanship...haven't thought about
that yet.

What do you think?
Do you agree with my "uncomfortable" feeling with the use of mutual
withdrawal as an "escape route"?

If so, what would be a nice way to leave all strategic options open,
but remove the option of "escape route"?
What do you think of my option?

W
